summary: Lower the implicit derived constructor when the base constructor signature and all construction sites are statically known.

target.notes: Emit a derived C# constructor that forwards the proven argument list to the base constructor. JavaScript's implicit constructor is effectively constructor(...args){ super(...args); }.

caveats: C# constructor signatures are static while JavaScript constructors accept dynamic argument counts.

tests.name: forwards known arguments
tests.input: class B { constructor(x) { this.x=x; } } class D extends B {} console.log(new D(7).x);

tests.name: edge: variable arity excludes direct constructor
tests.input: class B { constructor(...xs) { this.n=xs.length; } } class D extends B {} new D(1,2,3);
tests.expected_behavior: forwards all three arguments; this rule must not match unless rest/variable-arity construction is supported
